fields.v: Li, W., Xu, Z., Wang, Z., Yu, S., Zhu, W., Luo, Y., Xu, J., Wu, Y., Huang, H., Deng, K. (2026). WEAVE: Weaving Real-World Code Evolution into Dependency-Structured Tasks for Benchmarking and Training Code Agents. arXiv:2610.22039v3 [cs.SE], 20 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.22039v3 [cs.SE]; no published venue stated
Independent Researchers (W. Li, Z. Wang, Zhu, Wu, Huang, Deng); Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (Z. Xu); Tsinghua University (Luo); National University of Singapore (Yu, J. Xu)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — WEAVE framework that turns verified multi-PR histories into executable dependency-structured tasks (bounded PR DAGs via repository-calibrated typed change loci), the Graph Credit metric for dependency-consistent partial progress, WEAVE-Bench (300 tasks) and WEAVE-Train (3,200 tasks); four-part study: construction validity (RQ1), 8 models x 2 scaffolds on WEAVE-Bench (RQ2), SFT utility (RQ3), RL reward (RQ4)

No SDD approach. Configurations: agent scaffolds OpenCode and Cline (versions Not stated) x models Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.6, Kimi-K2.5, MiniMax-2.7. Training: Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B fine-tuned (SFT, GRPO) on WEAVE data vs Atomic-PR, Temporal-Window, SWE-rebench V2, daVinci-Agency

Benchmark instance I = (S_base, q, G, T_F2P, T_P2P, A): repository base state with the PRs reverted; unified task specification q consolidating the PR objectives (objective, scope and constraints, acceptance criteria; PR identifiers, commit metadata and historical details removed); dependency DAG G, F2P/P2P tests and test-to-node attribution kept evaluator-side, not shown to the agent

Benchmark construction: typed change loci extraction -> repository-calibrated coupling -> edge filtering and bounded DAG assembly (K = 8) -> executable task instantiation (reverse-topological revert or agent-assisted carve, F2P/P2P validation) -> node attribution -> train/bench split. Agent side: agent receives S_base and q and returns one patch (no prescribed phases)
None in agent runs. Humans: three expert annotators plus a senior adjudicator label candidate PR pairs for RQ1 ground truth
N/A (no SDD approach); full agent runs from a unified natural-language task specification
Not classifiable (task specifications consolidated from PR descriptions; authors do not use SDD terms; wording 'unified task specification')
Existing code bases: multi-PR feature, migration and fix tasks in real open-source repositories (base state with the target PRs reverted)

WEAVE-Bench 300 tasks (50 per language) from 52 repositories; WEAVE-Train 3,200 tasks from ~120 repositories; 2-8 PR nodes per task (bench mean 4.91, median 5); gold patch mean 378 lines (median 274), 8.4 files, 18.6 F2P and 142 P2P tests per task; RQ1: 30 repositories, 1,198 PRs, 219 gold edges
General open-source software (examples: Python web application, TypeScript monorepo); six languages: Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Java, Kotlin
N/A (no participants in agent runs). Annotators for RQ1: three 'expert annotators' and a senior annotator, background Not stated
Per-task interaction turns and total tokens (M) per configuration (Table 2); SFT training token budget (~158 M tokens) and token-scaling efficiency (~4x)

Resolved (all F2P tests pass, no P2P regressions; primary metric); Flat-F2P (fraction of attributed F2P tests passed); Graph Credit (dependency-conditioned partial credit, recursive minimum over the DAG); P2P regression rate (RL); SWE-bench Verified, Pro and Multilingual scores for trained models
None
None

OverCredit (phantom credit = Flat-F2P − Graph Credit); dependency recovery AP, Coverage, P@K (RQ1); Spearman correlation of scoring operators with Resolved; executable construction rate; randomized-graph control OverCredit

Automatic: test execution in isolated Docker containers, task-level macro averages, task-level bootstrap confidence intervals (stated), paired bootstrap with Holm correction for RQ1. Manual: expert labelling of PR pairs for RQ1 gold edges (Fleiss' kappa 0.791). Agent-assisted carve and agent-based test attribution used in construction where mechanical revert fails

RQ2, WEAVE-Bench, 300 tasks, one run per task (4,800 runs over 16 configurations). Criterion per task: Resolved = all F2P pass and no P2P regressions; no configuration-level success criterion stated by the authors. fields.v: RQ2: 300 WEAVE-Bench tasks; 16 configurations (8 models x 2 scaffolds); baseline: none (configurations ranked; flat scoring as baseline metric). Held constant: task specification, repository state, tool permissions, tool interface (shell + file edit), 200 turns, 2-hour task timeout, 30-minute test timeout; context window and temperature at provider defaults (not controlled); models via official provider endpoints. Acceptance tests: F2P/P2P tests from the PRs. Repetitions: one run per task per configuration. No human intervention. RQ1: WEAVE vs 4 single-signal baselines against 219 expert gold edges. RQ3/RQ4: matched token budget (~158 M) and matched rollout budget (8 rollouts per task), same generator, filter and training configuration

RQ2: Claude Opus 4.7 + Cline best (48.7% Resolved) vs MiniMax-2.7 + Cline worst (9.7%), >5x; Flat-F2P exceeds Graph Credit by 10.5 pp on average (7.2-16.8); Cline OverCredit mean 12.2 pp vs OpenCode 8.6 pp; random-graph control reduces OverCredit to 1.6 pp. RQ1: WEAVE AP 37.7% vs File Overlap 26.6% (paired 95% CI +2.7 to +20.1; p <= 0.009 vs all baselines after Holm), Coverage 84.5%. RQ3: WEAVE SFT +3.0/+3.7 pp Resolved over Atomic-PR at 4B/35B, +3.6/+2.8 pp SWE-bench Verified. RQ4: R_WEAVE +3.7/+4.3 pp Resolved over SFT, +2.0/+2.6 over flat F2P reward. Significance tests only for RQ1

Distinguished configurations (9.7-48.7% Resolved) and exposed phantom credit not seen by flat scoring; Graph Credit correlates better with Resolved (rho 0.82 vs 0.69 for linearized). Repeatability: one run per task per configuration, no variance reported for RQ2; SFT single seed (token-scaling curves 3 seeds). Limitations of the comparison method: no limitations section; scaffold settings left at provider defaults; ~35% of candidate DAGs discarded in construction

No limitations section. Gaps stated: single-PR task units capture only part of real development; multi-PR benchmarks use coarse aggregation and flat or binary scoring that over-credits downstream progress; binary rewards are sparse for RL. Caveats in text: AP < 20% in 3 repositories with < 5 gold edges; chain-dominated benchmark (median antichain width 1) limits differences between graph operators; depth vs OverCredit relation not established

Reporting inconsistency: in Table 2 several configurations report Resolved above Flat-F2P (OpenCode + Kimi-K2.5 14.0 vs 12.4, OpenCode + GLM-5.1 28.7 vs 24.1, OpenCode + GLM-5.2 34.0 vs 32.5, OpenCode + Claude Opus 4.6 30.3 vs 24.9, Cline + GLM-5.1 21.0 vs 18.8) although a resolved task passes all F2P tests; OpenCode mean OverCredit computes to 8.7 pp from Table 2 vs 8.6 pp in text. Bootstrap confidence intervals said to be reported but not shown for RQ2. Table 2 row/column layout jumbled by pdftotext (Kimi-K2.6 / GLM-5.1 values assigned by order). Replication package: no code or data link given; authors say the WEAVE-Train corpus 'can be published'. Pre-registration: none. Languages: Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Java, Kotlin. Corresponding author Ken Deng also authored KAT-Coder/KAT-V1 (Kwai) reports cited
